title: Lesson 94 - By This Time Next Year…

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: The record is complete: thirty-four people attended across four evenings. We spent seven hundred and forty-six dollars and used eighteen point two five extra staff-hours.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: So by the final review, we have completed everything the old framework authorized without crossing a ceiling.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: Yes. What stayed with me was the second evening’s cleanup. It ran twenty-five minutes beyond our estimate, although the next morning’s opener had not worked the event.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: I found the midpoint review effective because you removed the separate welcome-table setup before evening three. The final two cleanups then stayed inside the revised estimate.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: I wouldn’t say that proves the new setup will always work, but it gives us a recorded adjustment instead of a guess.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: What will have changed by this time next year even if we stop evening events?

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: By then, we’ll have added the preorder cutoff, final-number check and cleanup log to our daytime group-booking process.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: And staff will still be confirming any unusual schedule directly rather than being assigned through a general availability note.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: Correct. Those are process improvements supported by the trial; they do not depend on approving another evening program.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: We’re aiming to finish that daytime update by the end of next month, and we’ll know it is in use when three daytime group files contain the new checklist.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: If we approve no further evening service, by this time next year the four trial files will have been archived as a completed experiment.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: If we approve another bounded round, we may have collected more varied evidence by then, but staff will still be reviewing every date separately.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: A standing monthly service is different. At that point, we would be operating a recurring commitment, not repeating the same limited test.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: The current evidence does not support writing “we will be running monthly evenings next year.” That would announce a decision we have not made.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: Then the planning update should use two columns: outcomes expected under any option, and outcomes that depend on the final decision.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Good. By the end of the trade-off meeting, we’ll have chosen whether to stop, repeat a bounded test or propose a new recurring model.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: That choice could change if the record contains an error. I’ll attach the four attendance sheets, cost totals and signed rota confirmations for checking.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: What we don’t know yet is whether demand would continue beyond these groups or whether repeated evenings would remain within the same staffing margin.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: So the safest one-year statement is that we’ll have improved the daytime booking process and closed the old trial record; any new evening activity remains conditional.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Exactly. A future plan should show direction and checkpoints without turning an undecided branch into a promise.
